definitions.explanation: A pair of thin sticks used for eating, held in one hand. The polite form with the prefix お is the standard everyday term.

examples.japanese: お{箸|はし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
お{箸|はし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{持|も}ち{方|かた}→持ち方：28218_mochikata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦きれい→きれい：00717_kirei⟧です⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
⟦{割|わ}り{箸|ばし}→割り箸：09725_waribashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{箸|はし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}いて→付く：01960_tsuku⟧こないとき⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}います→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: You use disposable chopsticks when chopsticks aren't provided.

notes:
The お prefix is standard and not overly formal — most speakers say お{箸|はし} rather than just ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧ in everyday speech. Dropping the お sounds slightly rough.

MATERIALS AND TYPES:
- ⟦{割|わ}り{箸|ばし}→割り箸：09725_waribashi⟧ — disposable (split) chopsticks
- {塗|ぬ}り{箸|ばし} — lacquered chopsticks
- マイ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧ — one's own personal chopsticks (eco trend)

CHOPSTICK MANNERS (⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧): There are many taboos around chopstick use in Japan, including ⟦{刺|さ}し→刺す：02111_sasu⟧{箸|ばし} (stabbing food), ⟦{渡|わた}し→渡す：02442_watasu⟧{箸|ばし} (passing food chopstick-to-chopstick, associated with funeral rites), and {迷|まよ}い{箸|ばし} (hovering over dishes).
